title: A sixth person has died from an outbreak in NYC's air
text:
A sixth person has now died from an outbreak spreading through New York City's air, and it isn't a virus.

Legionnaires' disease spreads through mist from contaminated water systems, cooling towers, hot tubs, even shower heads, not from person to person. Health officials in the affected neighborhood say most cases can be traced back to airborne water vapor drifting from a handful of building cooling towers.

You can't catch it from a sick coworker. You catch it from breathing the wrong cloud of air.
